force.title: Atoms Strike Back
force.signature: Trade war and tariffs force reshoring, nearshoring, and inventory hoarding — physical supply chains get expensive and political, and whoever moves fastest to nearshore wins.

A \u00b7 The auto reordering: 2025 tariffs and the EV transition force the whole auto supply chain to reorder toward Mexico.
Electrification voids some parts and creates others; suppliers must pick a side.
B \u00b7 Heavy materials & metals: Steel and aluminum tariffs ripple into every downstream builder and maker.
Basic materials get repriced by tariffs, energy, and reshoring.
C \u00b7 Reshoring the factory: Defense, reshoring mandates, and supply-chain security pull advanced manufacturing home.
Durable-goods makers weigh tariff costs against nearshoring and automation.
D \u00b7 Food & the retail edge: Food processing and ag ride commodity and trade-war volatility.
Import-heavy retail eats tariff costs or passes them to shoppers.
E \u00b7 The big picture: Capstone: the physical supply chain got political; nearshoring and domestic makers win, thin-margin importers lose.
